title: Pre-Analysis — Windshield Heating Terminal Block and Interlayer Bus Bar Improvement
abstract: Original pre-analysis for the relocated terminal block and wider interlayer bus bar on the flight compartment windshield, closed clean with one wiring action and one manual revision.

sections.objective: Establish whether relocating the electrical terminal block and widening the interlayer bus bar of the heated windshield disturbs anything on the aircraft side of the interface, and whether the current density change alters the heating control behaviour. The delamination at the outer edge of the heated pane was traced to a local hot spot at the terminal block, and the work order had to confirm the fix does not simply move the problem into the cockpit panel harness that feeds it.
sections.findings_summary: Two aircraft-side items were confirmed and one soft result is worth recording. The cockpit panel harness that feeds the windshield heating is terminated on the same block and its strain relief is dimensioned for the present block position; moving the block by the proposed offset takes the harness outside its bend radius at one of the two positions, which the wiring office had not been asked about. The windshield installation task carries the terminal torque values and the continuity check that both change with the wider bus bar, and it is the working document for every pane change on the line. The soft result came from similarity alone: the bolted doubler repair for cabin window frame corner cracking describes an entirely different structure but records the same lesson about local stiffness change at a bonded interface, and its acceptance approach is worth borrowing for the pane edge.
sections.next_steps: Bring the wiring office into the design review to resolve the harness bend radius at the second terminal position before the block offset is frozen. Revise the windshield installation task with the new torque values and continuity check. Ask the flight compartment structures owner whether the pane edge acceptance can follow the approach already used for the cabin window doubler rather than inventing a new one. No effect on dispatch or on the heating control law was found.

similarity_seeds: local hot spot delaminating the outer edge of a heated pane
current density at an interlayer bus bar termination

tasks.title: Trace the harness feeding the windshield heating terminal
Review the pane installation acceptance content
Look for comparable bonded interface acceptance elsewhere

expected_findings.rationale: The cockpit panel harness terminates on the same block and its strain relief is dimensioned for the present position. The proposed offset takes the harness outside its bend radius at the second terminal, and the wiring office was not in the original scope.
expected_findings.resolution: Resolve the bend radius at the second terminal in the design review before the offset is frozen.

expected_findings.rationale: The installation task holds the terminal torque values and the heating continuity check. Both change with the wider bus bar and the task is used at every pane replacement, so a stale revision would be applied fleet-wide.
expected_findings.resolution: Revise the task in step with the modification effectivity.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity alone and by nothing else. The repair is a bolted doubler at a cabin window frame corner and the modification is an electrical termination change on a cockpit pane; no part number, zone, drawing or chapter is shared, and the titles have no word in common.

expected_findings.rationale: The repair records how a local stiffness change at a bonded interface was accepted on a transparency surround. The same acceptance approach applies to the pane edge after the bus bar is widened and saves inventing a new criterion.
expected_findings.resolution: Borrow the acceptance approach; no design or documentation action against the repair.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares the full windshield part set and both cockpit zones and is always returned next to the installation task. Removal disconnects the terminal without measuring it, so neither the torque values nor the continuity check appear in it and nothing in the task changes.

type_data.conclusion: The improvement is sound. One harness bend radius must be resolved in the design review and the installation task revised; no dispatch or control law effect.
